# Repository automation

The extra Dependabot rebase workflow is optional and disabled until the repository
variable `ENABLE_DEPENDABOT_REBASE` is set to `true`. Configure the dedicated token
described below before enabling it. Dependabot updates, audits and ordinary CI work
without that token.

CI cancels superseded checks. npm publication serializes the stable `latest` destination; release notes serialize each release without cancelling writes. Releases must be published stable `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` tags whose committed package identity and exact tag commit match a main ancestor. The pipeline does not rewrite versions.

Recovery uses the current main workflow and trusted main automation to verify and publish an existing published stable release tag: `gh workflow run npm-publish.yml --ref main -f tag=vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Replace the tag placeholder with the existing release tag. The validated exact-tag source receives frozen root and playground installs before full verification; recovery retains ancestry, identity, integrity, channel and provenance checks and never retags or changes versions.

Privileged scripts execute from trusted main, while release builds use the validated exact tag. Dependabot metadata executes trusted base code. Auto-merge verifies the current run/attempt, workflow identity and unchanged definition, bot-authored verified commits, exact head, and one digest-bearing minor/patch marker before approving that exact commit and enabling guarded auto-merge. Automatic reviews apply only to verified Dependabot minor/patch updates; major updates and ordinary PRs still require maintainer review. Artifacts are data, never executable publisher input.

Dependabot Rebase checks open Dependabot PRs with auto-merge enabled after main pushes and successful CI/auto-merge runs, plus every 15 minutes for recovery when token-created merges do not trigger another workflow. It requests `@dependabot rebase` only when the current main commit is missing from a same-repository bot branch with exclusively verified Dependabot commits. Dependabot then updates the branch and triggers fresh checks and metadata validation; branch protection still gates the merge. Requests from the authenticated account are deduplicated by the PR head and main commit for 30 minutes before retrying, and both heads are rechecked before each request. Major updates without auto-merge, human changes and forks are skipped.

Rebase setup requires an Actions repository secret named `DEPENDABOT_REBASE_TOKEN`. Use a fine-grained personal access token from an account with push access, limited to the intended package repositories, with Contents read and Pull requests write permissions. The built-in GitHub Actions app token is rejected by Dependabot comment commands even with contents write permission. The workflow token therefore stays read-only; the personal token is exposed only to the trusted rebase script step. Missing credentials and app identities fail before any rebase request is posted. Keep the token valid and rotate the secret before expiration.

Publication compares the packed tarball's SHA-512 integrity with npm, refuses version collisions, and verifies the resulting stable channel. Registry visibility is checked at most 61 times with five-second intervals: at most 300 seconds of retry delays, plus request time. Only absent artifact visibility or pending channel propagation is retried; conflicting identities, channel rollback, and registry errors fail immediately. Existing banner assets are reused only with a matching SHA-256 digest and are never clobbered. Managed release notes replace only their explicit marker section; author notes remain outside it. Concurrent author changes detected before an update cause a safe failure. GitHub does not offer an atomic body compare-and-swap through this API; maintainers should avoid simultaneous manual and automated edits.

PR title checks use read-only `pull_request_target` and trusted base code without a PR checkout. Checkout uses GitHub's event-pinned `github.sha` from the trusted default branch (`main`), rather than the potentially stale PR base SHA, so later metadata edits use current trusted automation. PR titles remain environment data; PR code is never checked out or executed. Workflow lint executes a checksum-verified actionlint installer from trusted base. CI scripts are TypeScript; shell only orchestrates download, checksum verification and extraction.

Dependabot covers root/playground Bun locks and pinned Actions, with a one-day version-update cooldown and minor/patch groups. Majors remain separate. Required labels must be provisioned before enabling label consumers: `dependencies`, `bun`, `github-actions`, `major`, `minor`, `patch`, `security`, `ci`. Cooldown does not intentionally delay security fixes. Security labels are assigned only to verified vulnerability fixes using platform metadata or maintainer review; the read-only metadata workflow does not write labels or infer security from SemVer. Existing CodeQL and redacted Gitleaks coverage remain in place.

Checks: `tsc --noEmit -p .github/scripts/tsconfig.json`, automation unit tests under `src/tests/automation`, actionlint, and shellcheck. Verify actual GitHub job and npm OIDC behavior after integration; local tests never publish or merge.

Commit-based notes classify `fix(security):`, `chore(security):` and `deps(security):` ahead of routine changes; labels alone do not alter generated commit categories.

Provider scripts follow responsibility: process orchestration in shell, structured validation/API logic in TypeScript. Shared repository identity is validated centrally by `scripts/lib/repository.ts`; release and dependency-update contracts live in their owning `Types/` directories. GitHub/event, registry and packed-artifact data are validated before use.

Before enabling publication, configure npm trusted publishing for `@rentnerkev/menu` with GitHub Actions as the identity provider, repository `RentnerKev/RentnerMenu`, and workflow filename `npm-publish.yml` (without the `.github/workflows/` prefix). The npm package must exist before its trusted publisher can be configured. This new package therefore needs a one-time initial publication using the package owner's npm login. Enable the trusted publisher's direct `npm publish` permission; the workflow does not use staged publishing. npm requires the first successful trusted publish within two days of creating the configuration. The release job uses npm OIDC through `actions/setup-node` and must not receive a long-lived npm token. Keep package access public and provenance enabled. The workflow only publishes on an explicitly published GitHub release or an explicitly dispatched existing stable tag; validate the npm trusted-publisher setup before the first release.
